sources.locator: Section 1.5 'Standard generators of the braid group', printed p. 7-8; section 1.6 'Braids as automorphisms of the free group', printed pp. 8-10 (PDF pp. 8-10), including Figure 3 (the loops x_1,...,x_n), the displayed formulas for rho_{sigma_i}, the braid-relation check, the paragraph identifying x_1...x_n with the boundary-parallel loop, and Theorem 1.3; section 1.6.1 'First solution to the word problem', printed p. 10; section 1.6.2 'Braids are residually finite and Hopfian', printed pp. 10-11 (read; not consumed).

contents.name: Section 1.5, standard generators sigma_1,...,sigma_{n-1} generate B_n
Section 1.6, Figure 3: the loops x_1,...,x_n are free generators of pi_1(D_n) drawn from a boundary base point
Section 1.6, the fundamental group of the n-times punctured disc is the free group of rank n
Section 1.6, a braid is a mapping class of D_n up to isotopy and acts on pi_1(D_n) by beta(gamma), giving rho: B_n -> Aut(F_n)
Section 1.6, the displayed formulas rho_{sigma_i}(x_i)=x_{i+1}, rho_{sigma_i}(x_{i+1})=x_{i+1}^{-1}x_ix_{i+1}, other generators fixed, with rho_{sigma_i^{-1}} deduced
Section 1.6, the check that the displayed automorphisms satisfy the braid relations so that rho is well defined
Section 1.6, notice that rho_beta sends each generator x_j to a conjugate of a generator
Section 1.6, x_1...x_n corresponds to a loop parallel to the boundary of D_n, so rho_beta(x_1...x_n)=x_1...x_n for every beta
Section 1.6, Theorem 1.3 (Artin): f in Aut(F_n) is rho_beta for some braid iff f(x_i) is conjugate to some x_j and f(x_1...x_n)=x_1...x_n
Section 1.6.1, first solution to the word problem by comparing the automorphisms rho_{beta_1}, rho_{beta_2} on generators and reducing words
Section 1.6.2, Theorem 1.4: B_n is residually finite and Hopfian (Magnus)
contents.reason: Residual finiteness and Hopfianity are separate Magnus consequences of the embedding B_n < Aut(F_n); no claim on this pair asserts or consumes them, and the page stops at the action, faithfulness and the word problem.

sources.title: Emil Artin, Theory of Braids, Annals of Mathematics 48 (1947), pp. 101-126
sources.locator: Theorems 13-16 with their full proofs, printed pp. 111-115 (article pages; complete journal PDF), including the substitution formulas (14) and (15) on pp. 113-114, the groupoid/substitution identification of Theorem 14, the necessary product condition of Theorem 15, and the two-case induction of Theorem 16 on pp. 114-115; the relations (18)-(19) on p. 115 (read; not consumed).

contents.name: Theorem 13, expressions (5) do not depend on the special braid-coordinate system
contents.reason: Artin's projection-coordinate expression (5) is an alternative encoding of a braid class; the scaffolded route identifies braid classes with mapping classes and their action on pi_1 instead, so no item consumes Theorem 13.

contents.name: Theorem 14, the groupoid of braid classes with end subsets of the X_i is isomorphic to the groupoid of substitutions
contents.reason: The pair proves faithfulness through the mapping-class action on the free group and the arc/Alexander straightening argument; Artin's groupoid isomorphism is an independent classical identification and is recorded here as a fallback, not consumed.

contents.name: The substitution formulas (14) defining sigma_i: t_i -> t_{i+1}, t_{i+1} -> t_{i+1}^{-1}t_it_{i+1}, other generators fixed, and (15) for the inverse
Theorem 15, a braid substitution fixes the ordered product of the generators
Proof of Theorem 16, case 1: no middle letter is affected, the residues are exactly t_1,...,t_n and the conjugators vanish
Proof of Theorem 16, cases 2(a) and 2(b): one of two adjacent middle letters is reached first and composition with sigma_i^{+-1} strictly shortens the substitution
Theorem 16, a substitution is a braid if and only if it has the general form of a transformation and satisfies the product condition; it is a product of the sigma_i
Relations (18)-(19) between the sigma_i and Artin's remark on the presentation
Theorems 17-19 (normal form, center) on printed pp. 116-126
contents.reason: The normal form and center theorems belong to the later Garside page of the braid track, which proves them from its own sources; this pair consumes only the automorphism formulas and Theorems 15-16.
